predecessors.name: County of Oldenburg
predecessors.text: Oldenburg as it stood in 1806: the county raised to a duchy, with Delmenhorst, the Münsterland round Vechta, the Weser bank and Eutin

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: the grand duchy, a state of the German Empire 1871-1918, with Birkenfeld, Jever and Eutin

ledger.x: 1806: the map begins with the Duchy of Oldenburg, the county raised to a duchy in 1774 (infobox; the body text says 1777).
1810: the Principality of Lübeck (Eutin) is annexed to France.
1813: William I is restored and the duchy returns.
1814: Eutin returns to the Duchy of Oldenburg.
1815: the duchy becomes the Grand Duchy of Oldenburg.
1817: Oldenburg takes possession of the Principality of Birkenfeld on 16 April 1817.
1818: Oldenburg annexes the Lordship of Jever.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: The French department of Bouches-du-Weser was divided in 1814 among Hanover, Oldenburg and Bremen; William I was 'restored 1813-23'.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: 'In 1866 he had sided with Prussia against the Austrian Empire during the Seven Weeks War'; Oldenburg lost and gained no land and joined the North German Confederation in 1867.

certainty.note: No page gives the duchy's boundary; it was a scatter of old counties and the 1803 gains.

Frontiers of a member of the German Confederation after the Congress of Vienna; Birkenfeld and Eutin are separate territories with their own frontiers; the pages record no change after the annexation of Jever in 1818.
